messages:
liz_finance: Quick follow-up from AH1: we mentioned a small contingency fund to avoid chopping critical projects mid-quarter. How will that be governed?
sam_ceo: Plan is to hold a centralized $500k contingency for the next two quarters. Itll be reserved for emergency SLA fixes, major security findings, or clear revenue protection. Use will require a 2-person sign-off (Finance + Exec).
omar_engineering: Is there a definition for 'emergency' vs 'nice-to-have'? Some infra work feels urgent but is actually optimization.
liz_finance: Good call. Emergency = immediate customer impact or compliance/security remediation that if not fixed would cause material harm within 30 days. Optimizations should be deferred or re-prioritized.
tess_prod: Related: any guidance on consolidating overlapping SaaS subscriptions? We have multiple analytics tools across teams.
sam_ceo: We want consolidation. FP&A will put together a vendor rationalization wave: teams should nominate redundant or low-usage vendors by next Tue. Procurement will run consolidation bids.
procure-bot: [automated] Vendor rationalization template: https://confluence.redwood.example/vendor-rationalization - submit list + usage metrics.
omar_engineering: For vendors with annual pre-pay discounts, does consolidation change the approval flow if it spikes near the $75k threshold?
liz_finance: Consolidation that increases contract value still follows thresholds. But consolidated deals will be fast-tracked for exec review to capture better pricing; include a migration plan and risk mitigation.
tess_prod: If a team wants to terminate a vendor mid-contract to move to a consolidated provider, are there penalties we should budget?
procure-bot: [automated] Check termination clauses before cancelling. Procurement can request termination cost estimates and include them in the business case.
sam_ceo: Action: teams nominate consolidation candidates + estimated termination costs by next Tuesday. Finance will evaluate net savings and runway impact.
liz_finance: Another small ask  BYOD and remote work stipendsshould they be treated as headcount cost or operating expense?
sam_ceo: Treat stipends as OPEX. They stay within the people ops budget unless a stipend program expansion pushes us materially off-plan.
omar_engineering: Final thought: if a critical experiment needs short-term infra spikes, is there a sandbox budget vs production budget split?
liz_finance: Keep experimental infra under a separate dev budget capped at $10k per team per quarter. Anything above gets moved to AMBER review.
tess_prod: Thanks. Will collate our vendor list and termination estimates.
sam_ceo: Appreciate it. Keep the bar high on what's mission-critical and include migration costs when proposing consolidation.
